problem:
Given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

 express the quadratic form $Q(x)=-{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-2{x}_{2}^{2}\,$ in terms of the components of $y.$

activity_context.topic_title: Change of Variables in Quadratic Forms

examples.knowledge_point: Changing Variables in a Quadratic Form Given Old Variables Through New Variables
examples.problem: Given that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066712/assets/57718ef2e6ecd26138c4c6a1b817d1129ad95a7473bf2e7d1611fdc64391e5c8.png) express the quadratic form $Q(\mathbf{x})= x_1^2-x_2^2\,$ in terms of the components of $\mathbf{y}.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, notice that  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066712/assets/12e6df2cc03a95228ac8d54512772c914f3283f1f62d814f2e996de67c93a041.png)

gives the following expressions for $x_1$ and $x_2\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={y}_{1}-{y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} & =2{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}-{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =({y}_{1}-{y}_{2})^{2}-(2{y}_{2})^{2} \\  & ={y}_{1}^{2}-2{y}_{1}{y}_{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}-4{y}_{2}^{2} \\  & ={y}_{1}^{2}-2{y}_{1}{y}_{2}-3{y}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
